references.text: Parallel account where Jesus utters the same words about the poor and his own presence at the institution of the Lord's Supper.
Mark's version of the event with the woman's anointing, with an identical quote that the poor are always present, but not Jesus.
Jesus quoted Isaiah about preaching the gospel to the poor, a central theme in John 12:8 where care for the poor is contrasted with Jesus' earthly time.
Psalm that highlights the blessing upon the one who has regard for the weak, a theme underlying Jesus' reminder of the presence of the poor.
Proverb linking mercy toward the poor to God's reward, which supports the context of treating the poor with respect in Jesus' words.
